y-m-64-06.title: How chance dey change as dem add information one piece at a time?
y-m-64-06.topic: Conditional probability: how chance dey change as dem add information
y-m-64-06.goal: Follow with counting cases how each time new information arrive, possible cases dey reduce and chance dey rise, remain same, or become 1.
y-m-64-06.material: Dem throw one red die and one blue die once each. Di two dice fair and no dey affect one another, and each face from 1 to 6 get same chance. If sum of both faces na 8 or more, dem call am 'success'. Dem never know result yet, and dem go give information piece by piece.

y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.0.r.b: Na estimate wey use middle sum, 7, as dividing line and think say na half and half. Di 6 ways with sum 7 no be success.
y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.0.r.c: Dis match value wey you get by counting cases with sum 8, 9, 10, 11, 12 and adding dem.
y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.0.r.d: Maybe na estimate wey feel say '8 or more' cover wide range among di 6 sums (7 to 12). Di bigger di sum, di fewer di cases.

y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.1.r.a: Dis match value from counting, among 18 ways with even sum, di 5 + 3 + 1 = 9 ways wey get sum 8, 10, 12.
y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.1.r.b: Information say sum na even reduce possible cases from 36 ways to 18 ways. You gats count again inside di reduced cases.
y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.1.o.c: E don smaller, to about one-third
y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.1.r.c: If you keep only cases with even sum, share of cases with sum 8, 10, 12 actually bigger. Count cases wey remain yourself.
y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.1.o.d: E don much bigger, to about 5/6 or more
y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.1.r.d: Cases with even sum still include sums 2, 4, 6. Plenty cases wey no be success still remain.

y-m-64-06.s.s1.st.2.after: Cases with even sum and different faces na 18 - 6 = 12 ways; among dem, successes na 9 - 3 = 6 ways. Chance na 6/12 = 1/2, e remain same. Di 3 success cases (4,4), (5,5), (6,6) comot together, so ratio no change.

y-m-64-06.s.s2.model.0: Among 6 cases with same faces, di ones with sum 8 or more na 3 cases (4,4), (5,5), (6,6), exactly half. Among 18 ways with even sum, success na 9 ways, half; so even after removing 6 same-face cases, success na 6 of di 12 ways wey remain, and ratio stay 1/2.

y-m-64-09.title: For dis situation, we fit treat number of successes as repetitions with same chance?
y-m-64-09.topic: Binomial distribution: situations where model fit and where e no fit
y-m-64-09.goal: Judge each situation what conditions dey needed to treat number of successes in repeated trials as binomial, and confirm with numbers how calculation result change when dem break conditions.
y-m-64-09.material: To treat number of successes as binomial distribution: (1) number of trials gats fixed, (2) each trial gats get one of two outcomes, success or failure, (3) chance of success gats same every trial, and (4) trials no gats affect one another. We wan check these four conditions for situations below. Box get 6 white balls and 4 black balls.

y-m-64-09.s.s1.o.d: Number of white balls wey come out when you repeat 5 times taking one ball, checking color, then putting am back
y-m-64-09.s.s1.r.d: Na choice wey check say because dem return ball, box state same every time.
y-m-64-09.s.s1.o.e: Number of questions answered correctly when you guess random for all 10 four-choice questions (questions no affect one another)
y-m-64-09.s.s1.r.e: Na choice wey check chance of getting each question right same and questions no affect each other.
y-m-64-09.s.s1.explain: For b, d, and e, number of trials fixed, chance of success each time constant, and trials no affect each other. For a, dem no return balls, so chance change each trial; for c, previous result change next chance, so trials affect each other.

y-m-64-09.s.s2.explain: Number of ways to choose positions for 7 out of 10 na 10C7 = 120, and chance of each na 0.6^7 × 0.4^3 ≈ 0.001792, so total na 120 × 0.001792 ≈ 0.215.
y-m-64-09.s.s3.prompt: For option a (take 5 without returning balls), chance all 5 be white, using binomial formula, na 0.6 to power 5 ≈ 0.078, but actual calculation na 6/252 ≈ 0.024. Explain why values different, connect am to conditions of dis situation.

y-m-64-09.s.s3.model.0: Because dem no return balls, share of white balls for box change each time dem take one. First na 6/10, but if white ball come out, next chance drop to 5/9, so e no fit be 0.6 every time. Trials no independent, and binomial formula come out bigger than actual value.

y-m-64-10.material: Class get 30 students. Minjun get 85 for math test and 72 for English test. Both tests total 100. We wan know which subject e do relatively better for class.

y-m-64-10.prereq.0: 'H1' for this task na only difficulty/support indicator for production assignment, no mean curriculum assign am to one school year. E assumes say you don learn normal distribution, mean and standard deviation for high school Probability and Statistics.

y-m-64-10.s.s1.prompt: Information dey revealed one piece at a time. Each time choose judgment about which subject Minjun do relatively better.
